messages:
emma: Heads-up — after the quantized 8-bit bring-up on rdx-quant we see a persistent small shift in BERTScore (~0.008 drop) for the summarization suite. Not huge but consistently reproducible across seeds. CI shows the regression started after the pass@k refactor.
rafa: :thinking: can you paste the exact eval job id and commit? also, did we switch tokenizers anywhere during the refactor?
emma: job=eval/2026-03-18/rdx-quant-01 commit=3f9b2c4. No tokenizer changes in model code, but the runner refactor moved metric computation into a separate process (metrics-runner) and I noticed it imports tokenizers from eval-harness instead of model repo.
sanjay: quick hypothesis: if BERTScore uses the wrong tokenizer (e.g., reference vs model), embeddings could be off by subword splits. small delta could be tokenization-driven not model quality.
maya: I ran a local diff of tokenizations on 100 examples: model tokenizer adds a leading space on <s> tokens, eval-harness tokenizer doesn't. That will change input ids marginally.
logan: that could explain the BERTScore delta but not the pass@k failing tests in CI — the CI diff shows pass@k numbers higher than local runs. Different seeds? different sampling logic?
emma: for pass@k I found something nastier. In metrics runner we compute pass@k as sum_{i} success_i / n where success_i is 1 if any of k samples match. but our harness uses an approximation that assumes independence and does a weird combinatoric:

```
# current buggy impl
p = 1 - comb(n - c, k) / comb(n, k)
```

where c is count of correct samples per example. That formula is only valid when sampling without replacement and the pool is set-based. But our sampling is with replacement (temperature sampling), so the approximation breaks when n is small.
rafa: ouch. so CI was running with the new harness where we treat n as sample_count and used comb, but local older harness computed exact by checking unique draws? or vice-versa?
emma: exactly — hosted CI uses sampling with replacement (the server uses sampler X), and the combinatoric comb() underestimates success probability when replacement allowed, leading to inflated pass@k in the comb formula relative to empirical runs.
sanjay: can you reproduce numerically for a toy case? need to show delta.
emma: did that. example: n=5 samples, c=1 (one success in the pool), k=3. correct closed-form for replacement sampling: 1 - ((1 - c/n) ** k) -> 1 - ((1 - 1/5) ** 3) = 1 - (0.8**3) = 0.488. comb formula: 1 - comb(4,3)/comb(5,3) = 1 - (4/10) = 0.6. So comb=0.6 > true=0.488 -> overestimates pass@k.
maya: nice repro. so CI overstates pass@k which explains some flaky green runs.
logan: action items: (1) make metrics-runner detect sampling mode (with/without replacement) and choose formula; (2) add unit tests for edge cases and small n; (3) fix tokenizer import path for BERTScore.
emma: I'll open a PR that (a) switches comb->replacement formula when sampler is with_replacement, (b) pins tokenizers to model repo for metrics that need model-specific tokenization, and (c) adds smoke tests to CI job. Drafting now.
rafa: also add an integration test that runs eval on tiny synthetic dataset where we can compute pass@k analytically, to catch regressions.
sanjay: one more gotcha — calibration step in metrics-runner does a histogram binning using sample counts from the aggregator, but aggregator was compressing float probabilities to 16-bit and occasionally clamping 1.0 to 0.9999 due to float16 rounding. That shifts expected calibration ECE by a tiny amount.
logan: ugh float16 surprises. where does aggregator downcast? I thought we're storing logits as float32 in the metrics db.
emma: metrics-aggregator has a compression path for large evals to save DB bytes: it stores probabilities as float16 and unpacks on read. We should avoid compressing probabilities used in calibration metrics or store summary stats instead of raw probs.
maya: proposed compromise: for calibration histograms store counts per bin (integers) and running sums of probabilities in float32; only compress raw sample traces, not aggregated calibration inputs.
emma: agree. PR will implement that and add a new test for calibration that compares float16 vs float32 behavior and asserts delta < 1e-4.
ci-bot: Deploy check triggered: metrics-runner/tests -> 12 tests failing locally (expected 0). See CI console: https://ci.internal/rdx/metrics/8762
emma: thanks CI. I'll iterate on tests. tagging @rafa for review when ready.
rafa: ping me when PR is up. also let's add a changelog note so oncall knows this affects pass@k semantics.
eval-bot: note: historical eval results (pre-fix) flagged as suspect. Recommend re-running release benchmarks after fix for stable baselines.
logan: we should schedule a short release-run for last week's model candidates after fixes. I'll put a calendar invite with "eval-harness: pass@k + tokenization fixes" for tomorrow.
emma: thanks all — working on PRs now. I'll paste links when ready. :thumbsup:
